inputs.prompt:
Using the reference images only as a STYLE guide, paint a new item icon. Do not copy their subjects or composition. The style is a ROUGH, QUICK CONCEPT ART SKETCH, like the references: bold, loose dry-brush strokes, visible bristle texture, chunky angular brushwork, scattered paint specks and splatter. Keep detail LOW: big simple shapes and flat planes of colour, blocked in with a few confident strokes. Suggest textures such as chain links, scales, engravings or stitching with a handful of broken strokes instead of drawing every piece. Edges may be rough and painterly. No polished rendering, no fine linework, no smooth gradients.

Item: The double-bladed steel head of a battle axe and the top of its wooden haft, diagonal
Use following color palette: dark iron and warm wood, burnt orange and deep crimson background

Composition: a CLOSE crop on the most recognisable part of the item (for example a sword's hilt and upper half of the blade, an axe head with the top of the haft, the upper torso of a coat from the collar down to the waist), so it fills most of the frame, roughly 80 to 90 percent. Only crop a little: the item may run slightly off the image border, but enough of it stays visible to read clearly what it is. It must stay readable as a tiny icon: one bold, simple shape with strong value and colour contrast against the background. The background is a burst of saturated brush strokes radiating outward from behind the item and filling all the remaining space edge to edge, with no empty dark or blank areas; the strokes stay behind the item and never cross over it. No hands, no mannequin, no stand, no other objects, no text, no border, no frame.
